questions.prompt: The circle with radius r is cut into equal wedges and rearranged into a shape close to a parallelogram. Its base is half the circumference. Write the base in terms of r.

questions.skill: Explain the relationship between the circumference and the area of a circle
questions.response: write the answer and show the required work
questions.prompt: The circle with radius r is cut into equal wedges and rearranged as shown. Explain how this shows that the area of a circle is πr².
questions.prompt_markup:
The circle with radius r is cut into equal wedges and rearranged as shown.
Explain how this shows that the area of a circle is πr².
questions.required_method: A complete argument: the rearranged shape is close to a parallelogram (a rectangle with more wedges); its base is half the circumference, {1/2} × 2πr = πr; its height is the radius r; so its area is πr × r = πr², and the circle has the same area because it is made of the same wedges. Any equivalent wording is accepted.

questions.prompt: Use the wedge argument to explain why the area of a circle is πr².
questions.prompt_markup: Use the wedge argument to explain why the area of a circle is πr².
questions.correct_answer: The wedges form a shape close to a parallelogram with base πr (half the circumference) and height r, so the area is πr × r = πr².

questions.skill: Give an informal argument for circle and volume formulas

questions.prompt: Two stacks of 20 identical coins have the same height. One stack is straight and one is slanted. Do they have the same volume? Explain.
questions.prompt_markup:
Two stacks of 20 identical coins have the same height. One stack is straight and one is slanted.
Do they have the same volume? Explain.
questions.correct_answer: Yes. At every height the cross sections have the same area (Cavalieri's principle).
